title: The weld keeps every attribute a batch shares and works on a clone of the cached scene; batching the rest of the base is wired and measured (2,024 -> 1,413 calls a frame) but stays off: with any newly batched landmark standing, the bloom's add stage paints the floor lattice as a cyan sheet, and the mechanism was not found
context: The owner, on the perf pass's finding that the static base is drawn as hundreds of calls a pass (2026-11-06-the-frame-at-the-owner-s-width-priced-the-one-pass-tail): 'do the two fixes and the batching'. The two fixes: mergeByMaterial (src/glbmodels.js) kept only position, normal and uv, so every batched model with COLOR_0 lost its vertex colours (18 live meshes under solar, bio-c, greenhouse, chips, ammo drew with vertexColors on and no attribute); and batchStaticAsset (src/fx/asset-batching.js) welded the loader's CACHED gltf.scene in place, so two landmarks from one file shared one root. The batching: batch: true on the dome city's six domes and four bridges and on hugin, stalheart, rotor, radar, launcher (keep: LAUNCH_SLED, CLAMP_L, CLAMP_R for src/fx/arc-launch.js), the four rockets and two wrecks; not the SH02 (the arrival scrubs its clips), the salvage (the foundry scraps its sections by name), the foundry (skinned), the bays (their hooks), the garage (its paint arm) and the pearls (their runtime). Written test-first (test/asset-batching.mjs, nine checks red then green). Branch perf-pass-2026-11-06, worktree ~/Dev/stalheart-perf.
outcome: LANDED: mergeByMaterial(root, pivots, exclude, { keepShared }) keeps an attribute every part of a batch carries at one item size (uv as before, now also color and a model's custom attributes), drops one a part lacks, and leaves parts apart rather than welding a colour of two item sizes; the other callers (the hull, the towers, the fabricator) pass nothing and weld as before. batchStaticAsset(source, clips, keepNames) welds a cloneSkinned copy, keeps the clip-driven nodes, TRACKER_TILT hinges and keepNames as their own objects, and keeps shared attributes; story-base mount passes each landmark's hide, dark and keep names. With only these on (the 13 structures batched as before), the picture is the main tree's and the suites below are green. MEASURED WITH THE FLAGS ON, headed at 1440x900, sector 2: draw calls a frame 2,024 -> 1,413 (the base's 1,232 -> 696 over 308 -> 174 objects; chain off 1,072 -> 804), CPU frame 10.6 -> 9.8 ms, GPU 19.7 -> 18.8 ms (noise), the launcher's five named nodes present, the domes' hidden port caps hidden, no mesh left with vertexColors and no colour attribute; the assembly line stays 605 meshes because its Assembly_Cycle animates 228 nodes (344 meshes under them) and the Stalheart's Terraforming_Cycle 49 (100 of 105), so a clip-heavy landmark gains nothing from the weld. NOT LANDED, THE FLAGS ARE OFF: with any newly batched landmark standing, the frame shows a pale cyan cellular sheet over the whole ground (the floor lattice, edgeMesh, drawn dense and bright, through the rock). Bisected on headless screenshots of the same page: the two fixes alone, clean; the dome flags alone, sheet; the base-layout flags alone, sheet; all flags: hiding the Story base group, or the twenty new holders, or the Stalheart's holder, or its near tier alone, removes it; hiding the Hugin, the domes, the sinkholes, the small line objects, or running ?creatures=dots leaves it; hiding the lattice removes it, hiding the rock brightens it. Through the chain's split: chain off, clean; pass A unweighted (noWeights), clean; pass A skipped (noPassA), clean; the mip chain skipped (noBloomPass), sheet; pass A on the screen (showPassA), clean; pass A's own buffer and the bloom texture copied to the screen before and after pass B (showA, showBloom, showAAfterB, showBloomAfterB), clean; pass B with the bloom blacked out (noAdd), clean; the add pass's own sampling of the bloom alone (bloomOnlyOut), clean; the scene added to itself (addSelf), brighter and clean; the scene plus pass A's buffer or plus the high-pass texture (addA, addBright), sheet; the old two-pass tail (separateAdd), sheet; three consecutive frames, stable. So the sum of two textures that are each clean on their own shows the thresholded lattice at full strength, only while a newly batched landmark stands, in the old tail as in the new: the leading reading is a texture-binding or state-cache desync in the add stage (the add sampling the high-pass or pass A target where it names the composite), and it was not pinned in this window. Every split is a postfx.tap mode now, so the next session starts from these screens.
alternatives: Shipping the flags with the sheet: no; the owner would see it on the first frame.
Batching only the landmarks that did not reproduce it: none did not; the dome flags alone and the layout flags alone both reproduced it, and with all flags the Stalheart alone carried it.
Keeping the old in-place weld of the cached scene: no; the clone is correct and the already-batched landmarks render the same (the headless census and the dome-look stills).
Dropping keepShared and keeping COLOR_0 only: a model's custom attribute (the pearls' _YUSHI) would still be lost; the intersection rule covers both.
evidence: test/asset-batching.mjs: nine checks, red before the change (colour dropped, the source scene welded in place, no named node kept), green after; node test/postfx.mjs green.

E, flags on, headed 1440x900 sector 2: chain on 50 fps 20.0 ms gpu 18.8 calls 1,413 tris 3.40M cpuFrame 9.8; chain off gpu 8.25 calls 804; Story base 696 calls / 174 objects (was 1,232 / 308); named { launcher: LAUNCH_SLED, CLAMP_L, CLAMP_R, PASSAGE_GATES, ACCELERATOR_LIGHTS all present; portCaps 32, 6 visible }; vertexColors without a colour attribute: 0 (was 18).

Headless screenshots in the session scratchpad (perf/): F-diag-batched (sheet), G-diag-noflags (clean), H1-domes-only and H2-layout-only (sheet), K-hide-base / -lines (clean), K-hide-planet / -newstructs / -oldstructs, M-hide-domes / -stalheart / -hugin, P-hide-stalnear (clean), U-hide-lines / -rock, U (noWeights, clean), W-hide-sinkholes (sheet), X-passA-flagged and Y-passA-unflagged (clean), Z-noBloomPass (sheet), Z-noPassA (clean), AC (noAdd, clean), AD-showA / AD-showBloom (clean), AF-f0..f2 (stable), AF (separateAdd, sheet), AG-addBright / AG-addA (sheet), AH-addSelf (clean), AI-showAAfterB / AI-showBloomAfterB (clean), AJ-bloomOnlyOut (clean).

The Stalheart's merged near tier, checked: 78 meshes, every geometry's index within its vertex count, no NaN, no coordinate over 200 m, world boxes 0.054-0.068 sphere units, MeshStandardMaterial throughout; the lattice shader's breach uniforms identical with and without the flags (count 2, holes [1, 1], radius 75.3).

Browser suites with the flags on: --dome-look green (stills show the sheet), --base-look green, --grow red (Isao said gunship_overhead), --antenna-print red (the near plane lowered). With the flags off (what is committed): npm test 334 programs green, npm run check green, --dome-look green; --antenna-print (the near plane lowered) and --grow (Isao said gunship_overhead) red exactly as on the untouched main tree e527eff4 run the same way, so they are the base's reds, not this change's.
